messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At a pressure of 10 kPa the equilibrium between solid ice and liquid water lies almost exactly on the same line that defines the normal freezing point at 1 atm.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice‑water transition (ΔHₘ ≈ 6000 J mol⁻¹, ΔVₘ ≈ −1.6 × 10⁻⁶ m³ mol⁻¹, Tₘ ≈ 273 K) gives  

\[
\frac{dP}{dT}\;=\;\frac{\Delta H_m}{T_m\,\Delta V_m}\;\approx\;-1.4\times10^{7}\ \text{Pa K}^{-1}
\]

so that a decrease of pressure from 101 325 Pa to 10 000 Pa (ΔP ≈ −9.1 × 10⁴ Pa) shifts the melting temperature by only

\[
\Delta T\;=\;\frac{\Delta V_m}{\Delta H_m}\,\Delta P\;\approx\;+0.007\ \text{K}.
\]

Thus the freezing point at 10 kPa is essentially the same as at 1 atm – roughly **0 °C** (about 0.01 °C higher, i.e., ≈ 273.16 K). In practice, the difference is far below the resolution of most laboratory measurements.
